sources.title: The Rust Programming Language: Understanding Ownership

outcomes.title: Trace a move
outcomes.observable: Name the valid owner after each transfer and predict a later use-of-moved-value error.

outcomes.title: Choose a shared borrow
outcomes.observable: Use a shared reference when the callee reads and the caller keeps ownership.

outcomes.title: Choose an exclusive mutable borrow
outcomes.observable: Use one mutable reference for bounded mutation and identify conflicting access.

outcomes.title: Reason about scope and validity
outcomes.observable: Identify when an owner is dropped and reject a reference that would outlive its value.

outcomes.title: Return a borrowed slice
outcomes.observable: Return a view into caller-owned data without copying or creating a dangling reference.

misconceptions.title: Assignment always copies
misconceptions.diagnostic: Uses both String bindings after assignment without clone or borrow.

misconceptions.title: A reference becomes an owner
misconceptions.diagnostic: Claims the borrowed value is dropped when the reference leaves scope.

misconceptions.title: Shared and mutable access can overlap
misconceptions.diagnostic: Keeps a shared reference live while mutating the same value.

misconceptions.title: A slice owns its elements
misconceptions.diagnostic: Returns a slice into a local value or treats a slice as an independent allocation.

diagnostic.prompt: After `let next = label;`, which binding owns the String?
A function only reads a String and the caller uses it afterward. Which parameter is narrowest?
A function appends to caller-owned text without taking it. Which parameter expresses that contract?
May a function return `&String` that points to a String created inside that function?
Which return type can expose the first word as a borrowed view?

lesson.title: Ownership is a changing responsibility
recallPrompts: Name the owner after each statement before reading the explanation.
State whether the callee needs to read, mutate, or keep the value.
Predict the compiler error code or successful postcondition before running Cargo.
lesson.summary: A non-Copy value has one current owner. A shared reference grants read access, a mutable reference grants exclusive bounded mutation, and a slice borrows a contiguous view. References never keep local owners alive beyond scope.

workedTrace.explanation: String allocation is owned by label.
Assignment moves the non-Copy String to next.
label remains a name but is no longer usable.
view reads next without taking ownership.
The borrow ends after its last use.

exercises.title: Inspect a job name
exercises.prompt: Implement `job_len` without cloning or taking the caller's String; accept the narrowest read-only borrow.

exercises.title: Inspect a table name
exercises.prompt: Implement `table_len` so a caller can append to its String after the call.

exercises.title: Choose move, shared borrow, or mutable borrow
exercises.prompt: Choose the parameter contract from the required postcondition; the item title does not name the strategy. Prefer &str over &String for read-only access.
exercises.solution: Select String, &str, or &mut String from the supplied postcondition, then pass value, &value, or &mut value accordingly. A shared read borrow should be &str: deref coercion lets callers pass &String, and the function accepts every string-like view.

exercises.title: Normalize a CSV header in place
exercises.prompt: Trim a caller-owned CSV header in place, then return its first column as a borrowed slice without allocating a second String.

Mark the owner before the call, during the parameter binding, and after return.

Change only the parameter type before changing the function body.
